description: Table 2 is a single-panel, two-row table rendered as an image; it contains no plot, axis, scale bar or legend, only printed text and numbers. The header row names four experimental conditions of the studied low-density steels, read left to right as: M1-SS, M1-30, M2-SS and M2-30 (SS = solution-treated, 30 = aged 30 h). The single data row is labelled "Grain Size (μm)" and gives one mean ± standard deviation value per condition: 42.4 ± 7.8 for M1-SS, 45.3 ± 9.3 for M1-30, 32.3 ± 10.4 for M2-SS and 35.8 ± 12.7 for M2-30. All four numbers are legible and can be read directly; nothing is inferred. Read across the columns, the table quantifies two comparisons: aging for 30 h leaves the grain size of both steels essentially unchanged (M1 42.4 → 45.3 μm; M2 32.3 → 35.8 μm), and the Ti- and V-added M2 steel is consistently finer grained than M1 in both the solution-treated and the aged state by roughly 10 μm. The table therefore supplies the grain-size evidence behind the claim that Ti and V addition refines the austenite grain size while aging does not alter it.

subfigures.description: Two-row table titled by its caption as Table 2, 'Grain size of experimental steels'. Header row: M1-SS, M1-30, M2-SS, M2-30. Data row 'Grain Size (μm)': 42.4 ± 7.8, 45.3 ± 9.3, 32.3 ± 10.4, 35.8 ± 12.7 respectively. No other rows or columns are present.

observations.observation: Table 2 has four columns headed M1-SS, M1-30, M2-SS and M2-30.
The single data row is labelled 'Grain Size (μm)'.
Grain size is 42.4 ± 7.8 μm for M1-SS and 45.3 ± 9.3 μm for M1-30.
Grain size is 32.3 ± 10.4 μm for M2-SS and 35.8 ± 12.7 μm for M2-30.
Within each steel, the 30 h aged condition has a slightly larger mean grain size than the solution-treated condition (M1: 42.4 → 45.3 μm; M2: 32.3 → 35.8 μm).
The Ti- and V-added M2 steel has a smaller mean grain size than M1 in both conditions (32.3 vs 42.4 μm solution-treated; 35.8 vs 45.3 μm aged).
The standard deviation of grain size is larger for M2 (10.4 and 12.7 μm) than for M1 (7.8 and 9.3 μm).
The caption states the table gives the grain size of experimental steels.
The citing text states that after aging the grain size of the M1 specimen shows no significant change, maintaining an average of 45.3 ± 9.3 μm, matching the M1-30 value in the table.
The citing text states that compared with M1 steel, the Ti and V-added M2 steel shows significantly refined grain size, and the grain sizes of M1 and M2 are listed in Table 2.

The citing text attributes an average equiaxed grain size of approximately 32.3 ± 10.4 μm to M2 steel; the table assigns that exact value to the M2-SS column and gives 35.8 ± 12.7 μm for M2-30, so the citation quotes the solution-treated M2 value.
